questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist resolved a criminal matter in another state by admitting to sufficient facts, and the case was continued without a finding and later dismissed. She tells the Board she has no conviction to report. How should that resolution be characterised for Board purposes?

choices.text: Not a conviction, because the case was ultimately dismissed by the court.
Not a conviction, because no sentence was ever imposed upon her.
Not a conviction, because the matter arose outside of the Commonwealth.
A conviction only if the Board separately finds that she committed the crime.
A conviction, because an admission to sufficient facts and a continuance without a finding are included.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is subject to two separate events: another state's board disciplines her nursing licence, and a week later she is criminally charged in Massachusetts. Which reporting statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Neither event is reportable until the criminal matter reaches a final disposition.
The out-of-state final action against her other health care licence must be reported within seven business days.
The out-of-state action is reportable only if it involved the practice of pharmacy.
The pending criminal charge must be reported to the Board in writing within 30 days.
Both events share a single 30-day reporting deadline.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist receives a Board request to appear and to produce dispensing records connected to a complaint. He is confident the complaint is baseless and simply does not respond. The Board later dismisses the underlying complaint. What is his exposure?

choices.text: No exposure, because dismissal of the underlying complaint resolves the matter.
No exposure, provided he can show the records would not have changed the outcome.
Exposure only if the Board issues a subpoena that he then ignores.
Exposure only if the underlying complaint had ultimately been substantiated.
Exposure, because failing without cause to cooperate is itself a ground for discipline.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is reviewing the range of actions the Board may take on a complaint. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: An advisory letter is retained in the Board's files but does not constitute formal disciplinary action.
Dismissal of the complaint is not among the actions available to the Board.
A reprimand constitutes formal disciplinary action.
A censure is a severe reprimand.
Probation allows practice under conditions imposed by the Board.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist negotiating a consent agreement is considering voluntarily surrendering her registration for a fixed period. Her counsel asks what the surrender document must say about later challenging it. What does the regulation require the agreement to state?

choices.text: That the surrender may be appealed to the Board within 30 days of the date it is signed.
That the surrender is reviewable by a court on the administrative record compiled by the Board.
That the surrender becomes final only after the Board publishes a decision in the matter.
That the surrender may be withdrawn at any time before reinstatement is formally sought.
That the surrender deprives her of all privileges of registration and is not subject to judicial review.

questions.stem: Another state disciplined a Massachusetts-licensed pharmacist for conduct that is lawful and consistent with good professional practice in Massachusetts and is not covered by any statutory protection. May the Board use that action as the basis for Massachusetts discipline?

choices.text: No, because that basis applies only where the conduct also violates Massachusetts law.
Yes, because any discipline imposed by a sister board is automatically actionable here.
Yes, provided the other state's process afforded the pharmacist a full hearing.
Yes, but only after the pharmacist exhausts every available appeal in that state.
No, because the Board may act only on conduct occurring inside the Commonwealth.

questions.stem: Another jurisdiction sanctioned a Massachusetts pharmacist solely for dispensing medication for reproductive health care services. The services would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with good professional practice here. The Board is considering discipline on the out-of-state ground. What is the correct outcome?

choices.text: Discipline may proceed, because out-of-state sanctions are a listed disciplinary ground.
Discipline may proceed if the Board first convenes an investigative conference.
Discipline may proceed but must be limited to an advisory letter in the file.
Discipline is deferred until the other jurisdiction resolves any pending appeal.
Discipline may not be imposed, because the protected activity carve-out overrides the listed grounds.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy learns that the Board is weighing urgent pre-hearing action against it. Which statements about the available mechanisms are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A hearing on the necessity of a Cease and Desist Notice must be afforded within seven days.
Where the Board suspends a licence prior to hearing, a hearing on the necessity of that action must be afforded within seven days.
Pre-hearing suspension requires a prior criminal conviction of the licensee.
A Cease and Desist Notice or Quarantine Notice is expressly non-disciplinary.
A Quarantine Notice may only be issued after a formal adjudicatory hearing.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist on duty knowingly lets a pharmacy technician perform final dispensing process validation during a staffing shortage. No patient is harmed and the prescriptions are all correct. What is the pharmacist's own exposure?

choices.text: No exposure, because no patient harm resulted from the temporary arrangement.
No exposure, because the technician holds a current Board technician licence.
Exposure only if the pharmacy failed to document the arrangement contemporaneously.
Exposure only if the Board first takes disciplinary action against the technician.
Exposure, because knowingly permitting activity beyond the authorized scope is a ground for discipline.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has received notice of an investigative conference. Which statements about Board disciplinary procedure are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: An investigative conference must precede any formal adjudicatory hearing.
An investigative conference is an informal discussion relating to a complaint held with the Board.
The Board may schedule an investigative conference at any time before a formal adjudicatory proceeding begins.
An Order to Show Cause orders the registrant to appear for a formal adjudicatory hearing.
A communication becomes a complaint once the Board determines, after investigation, that it merits further consideration or action.

questions.stem: A single incident at a Massachusetts pharmacy implicates both the pharmacist on duty and the pharmacy's own operations. The pharmacy argues the Board must choose one target. How should that argument be evaluated?

choices.text: It fails, because the Board may take disciplinary action against the pharmacist and the pharmacy alike.
It succeeds, because a single incident supports only a single disciplinary action.
It succeeds unless the Board first refers the matter to the Attorney General.
It succeeds, because entity credentials are disciplined only by the Department of Public Health.
It fails only where the pharmacist on duty is also the pharmacy's Manager of Record.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy intern is found to have violated state drug regulations during his internship. He assumes the worst outcome is a sanction on his intern licence and that he can still sit for licensure. How should he be advised?

choices.text: He is correct, because examination eligibility turns only on degree and internship hours.
He is correct, unless the violation involved a controlled substance.
He is correct, because NABP rather than the Board controls examination access.
He is wrong, because any regulatory violation permanently bars licensure here.
He is wrong, because the Board may prohibit him from taking the licensure examination as well.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is designing a pathway for staff to qualify as pharmacy technicians. Which statements about Board-approved training are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Any training program lasting at least one calendar year automatically qualifies.
A generic Board-approved program must include a minimum of 120 hours of theoretical and 120 hours of practical instruction.
A program provided by a branch of the United States Armed Services or Public Health Service may qualify.
An on-the-job training program may be used only if the pharmacy first obtains a Board waiver.
On-the-job training guidelines must be provided to the Board on request.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is preparing staff for the Board-approved pharmacy technician assessment examination. Which knowledge areas does the regulation require the examination to cover? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Laws and regulations regarding the practice of pharmacy and patient confidentiality.
The duties and responsibilities of a pharmacy technician in relationship to other pharmacy personnel.
Sterile compounding gowning procedures and aseptic technique.
Medical abbreviations and symbols.
Identification of drugs, dosages, routes of administration and storage requirements.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts school of pharmacy launches a new clinical pharmacy program and tells students their participation will count toward the internship requirement. What does the regulation actually require before that credit is available?

choices.text: The school must submit a written program description and the Board determines creditability.
Nothing further, because clinical pharmacy is already a listed internship setting.
Each student must individually petition the Board for credit after completing the program.
The program must be separately accredited by ACPE before any credit is available.
The preceptor must certify the hours, after which internship credit follows automatically.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts licensure applicant submits an examination application missing the required proof of date and place of birth, together with the full fee. The Board declines to consider the application. He asks whether he will get his fee back. What is the correct position?

choices.text: The fee is refundable because the application was never substantively evaluated.
The fee is refundable on written request within 30 days of the Board's decision.
The fee is held as a credit against his next licensure application.
The fee is refundable only if the omission resulted from the Board's own error.
The fee is non-refundable once the application has been reviewed and acted upon.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist obtained a duplicate certificate of licensure after losing the original. Months later the original turns up in a moving box. What does the regulation require her to do?

choices.text: Retain both and present whichever the Board requests.
Return the recovered original to the Board and keep the duplicate.
Promptly return the duplicate certificate to the Board.
Destroy the original and note the destruction in her records.
Report the recovery at her next renewal and keep both.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist teaches the same Board-approved continuing education program four times in one year and separately completes two courses in a postgraduate pharmacy curriculum. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: As a Board-approved instructor she receives credit for the program taught on a one-time basis annually.
She receives separate instructor credit for each of the four presentations.
Postgraduate credit is available only for courses in pharmacy law.
Postgraduate course credit requires the sponsor or co-sponsor to be Board-authorized or ACPE-accredited.
Postgraduate credit requires the course to instruct in pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, pharmacy practice or pharmacy law.

questions.stem: A provider is preparing two Board approval requests: one for a home-study program and one for a live program. Which statements about the Board's criteria are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A home-study program must contain a test to indicate progress and verify completion.
A home-study program must involve the learner by requiring an active response and providing feedback.
A live program shall involve direct interaction between the faculty and participants.
A live program must also supply a bibliography for continued study as a condition of approval.
Participants shall be given the opportunity to evaluate faculty, learning experiences and facilities.

questions.stem: At a busy Massachusetts pharmacy a patient accepts the offer to counsel on a new prescription. The only personnel free are a certified pharmacy technician and a pharmacy intern; the pharmacist is verifying another order. Who may deliver the counseling?

choices.text: The certified pharmacy technician, because certification covers patient communication.
The certified pharmacy technician, provided the pharmacist reviews the encounter afterwards.
Neither of them, because only the pharmacist personally may counsel a patient.
Either of them, because both may relay the pharmacist's offer to counsel.
The pharmacy intern, because counseling shall be made by a pharmacist or a pharmacy intern.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy assigns front-counter staff to make the offer to counsel at pickup so the pharmacist can stay at the verification station. What does the regulation require of that arrangement?

choices.text: The pharmacist shall ensure the designee is appropriately trained to make the offer to counsel.
The designee must hold a pharmacy technician licence before making any offer.
The arrangement is prohibited, because only a pharmacist may make the offer.
The designee must document each offer in the patient profile at the time it is made.
The arrangement requires prior written approval from the Board of Registration.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts patient collects a refill of an anticoagulant after a recent dose change communicated by the prescriber. A technician tells the pharmacist that counseling is not required because the prescription is a refill rather than a new drug therapy. How should the pharmacist respond?

choices.text: Agree, because the counseling duty attaches only to a prescription for new drug therapy.
Agree, provided the patient was counseled when this drug was first dispensed to her.
Agree, unless the patient affirmatively requests counseling from the pharmacist at pickup.
Disagree, because every refill of any prescription requires counseling without exception.
Disagree, because counseling is also required where the therapy is significant for the patient's health and safety.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is counseling a patient on a new inhaled therapy. Which items does the regulation identify as information counseling may include? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacy's wholesale acquisition cost for the medication.
Special directions and instructions for preparation, administration and use by the patient.
Techniques for self-monitoring drug therapy.
Proper storage and disposal of the medication.
Action to be taken in the event of a missed dose or adverse reaction.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy builds a private, well-signed consultation room with solid walls and a door. The only way a patient can reach it is by walking through the prescription dispensing area. Does the room satisfy the regulation?

choices.text: Yes, because the room provides adequate visual and auditory privacy.
Yes, because a staff escort accompanies each patient through the area.
Yes, provided the dispensing area is not visible from the store corridor.
No, because a consultation area must be located outside the pharmacy department.
No, because the area must be accessible without the patient traversing the dispensing area.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy with two separate dispensing windows is reviewing its counseling-rights signage. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A single sign at the store entrance satisfies the requirement for the whole pharmacy.
The letters may be any size provided the sign is legible from the counter.
A sign must be posted conspicuously adjacent to each area where prescriptions are dispensed.
The sign must be at least 11 inches in height by 14 inches in width.
The sign must be printed in both English and Spanish.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts community pharmacy is reviewing three practices: opening the front store an hour before a pharmacist arrives while filling nothing, omitting a measuring device for an adult liquid antibiotic, and applying its counseling policy to its affiliated inpatient service. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Counseling must be available at all times when the pharmacy is open for business.
The measuring-device duty applies only to paediatric liquid medications.
A proper measuring device must be dispensed or recommended with all liquid medications.
The inpatient exclusion removes just the offer requirement and leaves the rest of the section in force.
247 CMR 9.18 does not apply to pharmacists while practising in an inpatient setting unless otherwise required.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist receives an unusual prescription and telephones the prescriber, who confirms he wrote it. Which determinations must the pharmacist still make in the exercise of professional judgment before filling? Select all that apply.

choices.text: That the prescription was issued for a legitimate medical purpose by a practitioner acting in the usual course of professional practice.
That the patient has no outstanding account balance with the pharmacy.
That there is a valid patient-practitioner relationship.
That the prescription is authentic.
That the dispensing is in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, § 19(a).

questions.stem: A newly hired Massachusetts pharmacist dispenses medications reported to the Prescription Monitoring Program. Her pharmacy holds an institutional MassPAT account that the Manager of Record administers. What does the regulation require of her personally?

choices.text: She shall register with and maintain login information for the monitoring system.
Nothing further, because the pharmacy's account covers all dispensing staff.
She must register only if she dispenses Schedule II controlled substances.
She must register within 30 days of her first Board disciplinary contact.
She must register only if the Manager of Record delegates monitoring duties to her.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy offers a nursing home's administrator free catering for staff events. Nothing is said about individual patients, but the pharmacy hopes the facility will send it more business. How does the regulation treat the arrangement?

choices.text: Permitted, because no referral of any individual patient is being solicited.
Permitted, because catering is not a payment of money.
Permitted if the facility discloses the arrangement to its residents.
Permitted if the value stays below the pharmacy's ordinary annual marketing budget.
Prohibited, because a licensee may not offer anything of value for the generation of business.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts clinic pharmacy that does not hold a Drug Store pharmacy licence is asked to fill a prescription for the adult sibling of a clinic employee. The sibling lives across town and is not a clinic patient. May the pharmacist dispense?

choices.text: No, because the permitted recipients do not extend to that relative.
Yes, because the family members of employees are always covered.
Yes, provided the prescription was written by a clinic practitioner.
Yes, provided the sibling pays the usual and customary retail price.
Yes, because the restriction applies only to controlled substances.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts collaborating pharmacist is negotiating an agreement that will include prescriptive practices. Which additional conditions attach because of that inclusion? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Holding at least $2,000,000 per occurrence of professional liability insurance.
Maintaining a current controlled substance registration issued by the Department during the term of the agreement.
Completing at least ten additional contact hours of continuing education each year of the agreement.
Submitting an attestation under the pains and penalties of perjury regarding MassHealth participation.
Obtaining a separate Board licence category for collaborating pharmacists.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts collaborating pharmacist completed her required collaborative practice continuing education two years ago and her current agreement was signed six months ago. She proposes to discard the older documentation. What does the regulation require?

choices.text: She may discard it, because the courses are now more than two years old.
She may discard it once her pharmacist registration has been renewed.
She must retain it for at least two years after the date of the current agreement.
She must retain it for the entire life of her pharmacist licence.
She must forward it to each supervising physician instead of retaining it.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts collaborating pharmacist resolves a Board matter by consent agreement that places a condition on her practice. She works under collaborative practice agreements with three supervising physicians. What does the regulation require her to do?

choices.text: Nothing further, because a consent agreement is not a Board order.
Notify only the physician whose agreement relates to the conduct at issue.
Notify the Board that the physicians have been informed, without contacting them.
Provide written notification of the discipline or practice restriction to each supervising physician.
Suspend all collaborative practice until the condition has been lifted.

Do not open data/questions/, data/rules/, the authoring report, the post-lock reveal, the generated site payload, the controller ledger, the plan issue or any git history for these questions before that lock is committed.
content_boundary: Contains only question ID, type, stem and choices plus non-substantive package identity metadata. Excludes keyed answers, explanations, choice analysis, rule and drug identifiers, area, topic, subtopic, difficulty, family, provenance and all author reasoning.
